```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B names a payer (a non-engineering team lead or builder paying per workspace). A states plainly that there is 'No defined payer yet' and has no evidence of an institutional buyer. A defined payer matters most when the goal is a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "B's price anchors are higher and closer to its target buyer: display.dev Solo at €15, Pro at €49, Enterprise from €499, and Volly Team at $75 per workspace. A's anchor is a consumer subscription at $8–20 per month. Against A's own cited acquisition costs ($20–50 per user via ASO), that price makes payback hard. One or two workspace subscriptions is a more reachable 90-day milestone than recouping consumer acquisition costs.",
    "B's cited channels cost little or nothing: Product Hunt at about $3–5 CPA, Show HN at $0, and free marketplace listings. They also reach builders who already use agents. A depends on app-store acquisition, and its own brief calls the cost hard to recoup at $8 per month.",
    "Both ideas face crowded markets. A's competitors include free and credentialed products (Noora is free and Stanford-backed; SpringSocial and Talkville are free or in-app purchase). These directly reduce what customers will pay. B's competitors mostly show paid tiers, though one (Orb) is free-only, and they lean on the same pitch rather than being free.",
    "A carries extra non-technical risk. Professionals are skeptical of its efficacy (r/slp), it raises health-claim and minors' data issues if it targets autism or anxiety users, and that reputational risk is hard for a solo operator to manage. B's main risk, sandbox security, can be narrowed by keeping the product thin and starting with static or artifact hosting."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's revenue model rests on a payer that does not exist yet. The $8–20 per month hypothesis is anchored to Yoodli's tiers, but Yoodli is positioned around enterprise distribution, not the niche social-skills segment A would target. The one niche price point (Convo at about $8) is inferred from a single user review, and the brief found no official pricing page. A's demand quotes show people using or wanting AI practice, not paying for it.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Neither brief has strong independent demand evidence. B's best demand quote is a vendor-curated testimonial on Volly's own site, and its Reddit quote shows a sharing pain, not willingness to pay. B's claim that display.dev and Volly are 'monetizing' rests on published pricing pages, not revenue data, and Volly's paid plan is still in beta. B also carries real security liability for a solo operator. B wins mainly because it has an identifiable payer, higher price points, and cheap channels, not because its demand is proven."
}
```
